scope: Correction of historical gradient comparison and normalization direction; historical sources only. Current goal and hourly automation stay paused.

observations.native_scale_bound_scope: Q=g/s_u on original masked native policy positions, one TextCraft reward event; |g|<2.475 for official eight-trajectory binary rewards. The .0005 subtraction is console rounding uncertainty, not a new tolerance.

Q=g/s_u on original masked native policy positions, one TextCraft reward event; |g|<2.475 for official eight-trajectory binary rewards. The .0005 subtraction is console rounding uncertainty, not a new tolerance.

norm_scope.original: First-returned rank local pre-clip DTensor shard norm, not full gradient norm.
norm_scope.limitation: Historical simultaneous all-rank v6 norms were not stored in examined receipts; do not convert this prediction into measured global equivalence.
norm_scope.official_update_weight: Global64/B4 has16 original microbatches: 2GPU uses8 accumulation per rank and2-way mean; 8GPU uses2 accumulation and8-way mean. Both original total weighting1/16.

normalization.same_input_exact_scale_ratio: A6/A5=s5/s6 for nonzero entries, same native masks and original row weights.
normalization.direction: Relative to v5, v6 shrinks if s6>s5. Neither official group normalization of g nor separate normalization of u guarantees variance(g*u)=1. Absolute 1/s6 and relative s5/s6 are different quantities.
normalization.v6_population: Pre-multiplier unit-credit statistics include original zero-g trajectories; v5 final g*u has zero entries there.
normalization.missing_evidence: Exact retained-batch s5 and s6 on the same historical input were not saved in the examined v6 receipts. Do not claim the complete observed gradient difference has been decomposed.

corrections: Comparing raw two-GPU and eight-GPU shard norms is not an experiment measuring reduction of total gradient.
A smaller v6 gradient than v5 does not prove the absolute v6 normalizer is below1; native Q logs instead bound it above1 across these observed iterations.
The previous recommendation to restore normalization was a proposal, not a verified repair; no implementation follows from this analysis.
